study type: case-control with a prospective validation cohort
exposure: maternal risk factors (body mass index <18.5 kg/m2, nulliparity, tobacco use, absence of high school diploma)
cohort: The study included a case-control group of 438 pregnancies (82 PPROM cases, 64 preterm labor with intact membranes cases) with blood samples collected at first trimester, second trimester, and delivery, and was confirmed by a second independent prospective cohort.
finding: First trimester serum CX3CL1/Fractalkine levels were significantly increased in PPROM cases, making it a promising early predictive biomarker for PPROM, particularly when combined with maternal risk factors.
